function.name: EventSettingsApi_create_website_alert_config
function.description: Creates a configuration for website alerting within the system, allowing users to define conditions under which alerts should be triggered for a website. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The name for the website alert configuration.

description.description: A detailed description for the website alert configuration.

severity.description: The severity level of the alert when triggered.

triggering.description: Flag indicating whether the alert configuration should also trigger an incident.

websiteId.description: The unique identifier of the website for which the alert configuration is created.

tagFilterExpression.description: A boolean expression used to filter the scope of website beacons based on tags.

granularity.description: The evaluation granularity in seconds used for detection of threshold violations.

rule.description: The type of rule this alert configuration pertains to, such as 'traffic spike' or 'downtime'.

threshold.description: The threshold value that, when exceeded, will trigger the alert. This is a float type value.

timeThreshold.description: The time duration in seconds during which the threshold must be exceeded to trigger the alert.

alertChannelIds.description: A list of alert channel IDs defined in Instana to which the alert notifications will be sent.

Instana exposes its public REST‑API under a **versioned path**:

| Path Prefix | What it means |
|-------------|---------------|
| `/api/v1/…` | The *stable* production API. All core functionality—metrics ingestion, topology discovery, incidents, dashboards, etc.—is available here. |
| `/api/v2/…` | A newer “preview” layer that adds additional fields and capabilities (e.g., richer query options, more granular filtering). It isn’t yet fully backward‑compatible with all legacy clients. |

So, unless you’re explicitly targeting the experimental features, your integrations should point at **`https://<instana-host>/api/v1/*`**, i.e. **API v1**. If you see references to `v2`, those are usually meant for future‑proofing or advanced usage scenarios.
